title: The Dessert Nobody Asked For
scene: At a movie night, a homemade dessert turns out surprisingly salty, and the friends rescue the evening with dry humor.
sceneJa: 映画鑑賞会に持参した手作りデザートがなぜか塩辛い。友人の真顔の冗談に救われ、アイスクリームで仕切り直す。

chunks.ja: 手作りのデザートを持っていった
ちょっと得意げな気分で。
最初の一口は問題なかったけど、

chunks.en: I'd mixed up the sugar and salt jars
chunks.ja: 砂糖と塩の容器を取り違えていたらしい、

chunks.en: My friend kept a straight face
“Well, that's one way to cut back on dessert.”
chunks.ja: 「まあ、デザートを減らす方法としてはアリだね」。

chunks.en: and we ordered ice cream instead,
chunks.ja: 代わりにアイスクリームを注文した、

chunks.en: which was probably for the best.
chunks.ja: 結果的にはそれでよかったと思う。
誰もレシピを聞いてこなかった、

chunks.en: and I can't say I blame them.

questions.question: Which is the most natural chunk boundary?
options: It / turns / out I'd mixed up
It turns out / I'd mixed up the sugar and salt jars
It turns / out I'd / mixed up
questions.explanation: It turns out introduces a surprising discovery; mixed up stays together as the verb phrase.

questions.question: What does 'kept a straight face' mean?
questions.explanation: To keep a straight face is to avoid showing amusement, often while joking.

questions.question: Why does the friend say 'that's one way to cut back on dessert'?
options: To gently joke about the salty dessert
To praise the recipe as healthy
questions.explanation: The remark uses dry humor to ease an awkward moment.

speak: In 30 seconds, describe a food mistake: what you intended to make, what went wrong, and how someone made the situation funny. Use 'It turns out' and 'for the best'.
review: New: It turns out（実は〜と分かった）, keep a straight face（真顔を保つ）, for the best（結果的によかった）. Review: I couldn't help laughing（思わず笑った）, For what it's worth（一応言っておくと）. Read aloud: pause after 'It turns out' and deliver the joke with a flat tone.
